verdict.rationale: OpenCode uses a client-server design: `opencode serve` exposes an OpenAPI HTTP server, and the TUI and WebUI attach to that backend as clients. That strongly implies the UI is built on the same API, so it can be driven programmatically, including through a type-safe JS/TS SDK. A published openapi.json was also confirmed by probe. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement of full UI/API parity, endpoint-level documentation showing every UI action (e.g. sharing, agent switching, permissions) is API-reachable, independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The opencode serve command runs a headless HTTP server that exposes an OpenAPI endpoint that an opencode client can use.
Use it to build integrations and control opencode programmatically.
Attach a terminal to an already running OpenCode backend server started via `serve` or `web` commands.
This allows using the TUI with a remote OpenCode backend.
